purpose: Provenance registry for 3D assets generated for the MUSE-UM pavilion. A generated asset is an environmental prop: it never replaces a framed exhibit PNG, and it never changes a room's evidenceStatus.

generator.pipeline: Two routes. Text to 3D (two stages: preview geometry, then refine texture) for props that can be described. Multi-image to 3D (fused: geometry and texture from the same reference views) for props whose material language has to come from the pavilion's own art rather than from a prompt, since that endpoint accepts no prompt at all.
generator.note: Generator task IDs are recorded so the exact lineage of every accepted artifact is checkable.

curationGate: A task reaching SUCCEEDED is not acceptance.
Every artifact is reviewed as a rendered image before download.
An artifact is accepted only against its own tiered criteria in assets/meshy/<asset>.json.
Rejected artifacts are logged with the defect that failed them, not silently regenerated.

assets.role: environmental prop standing on the Observatory floor

inspection.optimization: gltf-transform optimize — meshoptimizer simplify, quantization, textures resized to 1024 and converted to webp. Lossy: the delivered mesh is not vertex-identical to the generated one.

acceptedProperties: Four rings crossing on different axes in open space, with no drum, cage or struts between them.
Central sphere present; silhouette reads as a celestial measuring instrument.
Warm aged brass with patina and wear; dark stone base.
Base is plain and unmarked — no lettering, numerals, plaque or inscription anywhere.
knownLimitations: The generated brass reads semi-gloss. The pavilion applies a higher roughness and a locally rendered environment in-engine rather than regenerating for finish.
Engraved star marks did not survive as clearly as the graduation tick marks on the outer band.
assets.reviewNote: Five generated passes were rejected before acceptance: two for invented pseudo-inscriptions that turned out to be geometry rather than texture, one for condensing the four rings into a concentric drum cage, and two superseded refinements. All are logged in the asset spec's reviewLog.

evidenceStatus.note: The armillary is the pavilion's own interpretation of the recorded observatory motif. Its source attachment lives on the Observatory room, not on this prop. The prop asserts nothing about a physical town artifact.

assets.role: recurring hanging fitting, identical in every room — provides pooled warm light and the pavilion's primary depth cue

inputLineage.styleAnchor: public/art/keepers-room.png — the exhibits' own lanterns, so the fitting is congruent with the art rather than merely plausible
inputLineage.note: The endpoint accepts no prompt. These reference views are the entire style input; the brief and the anchor image are therefore part of the asset's provenance.

inspection.optimization: gltf-transform optimize — simplify, quantization, textures resized to 1024 and converted to webp. Lossy: the delivered mesh is not vertex-identical to the generated one.

acceptedProperties: One coherent lantern — no merged blobs, doubled parts or exploded geometry.
Hexagonal cage with six vertical corner posts, tapered hexagonal roof, base finial, top hanging ring.
Warm aged brass with patina; no magenta contamination in the baked base-colour texture (measured 0.00%).
Panels read as solid opaque frosted surfaces, not open frames.
No lettering, numerals or invented inscription.
knownLimitations: Reads as a clean mid-level game asset rather than a photographed relic: the hanging ring and finials are thin, and the panes are flat.
The reconstruction carries no flame or inner light — glazing is opaque and no candle was modelled. The pavilion supplies the glow in-engine with an emissive lift and a point light below each body.

The warm gold of the lamp light measures as slightly off-token: room palette share fell from 83.6% to 79.8% with the fittings lit, still above the 77% floor. Warmth was chosen over a marginally higher share.
assets.reviewNote: Three build passes. v1 was rejected on material: briefed translucent glazing reconstructs as nothing, so the panes arrived as open air. v2 was rejected as a pink lantern — the sheet was delivered with transparency, the slicer flattened it onto the briefed magenta, and 22.3% magenta-family pixels survived into the submitted views and were baked into the texture. Both the slicer and the sheet brief were corrected: magenta is now keyed out and the written file is re-measured before submission, and the slicer refuses an input modified in the last 12 seconds because v2 was sliced while the generator was still writing it.

evidenceStatus.note: A pavilion fitting, not a claim about any recorded town artifact. It carries no source attachment and asserts nothing historical; the rooms' own source attachments are unaffected.

assets.role: architecture — a doorway at the room edge giving the space a way out and a sightline through it

inputLineage.styleAnchor: public/art/threshold.png — the pavilion exhibit that already contains an archway

inspection.optimization: gltf-transform optimize — simplify, quantization, 1024px webp textures. Lossy.

acceptedProperties: True through-hole with the backdrop visible through it, not a filled panel.
Jambs, a semicircular arch of separate voussoirs, and a prominent keystone.
Thick masonry with visible side faces; not a flat card.
Carved chevron band on the arch face; low threshold step.
Warm tan/umber stone, no key-colour contamination, no lettering.
knownLimitations: Reads as a freestanding surround rather than part of a full building.
Placed at the room edge, where it is partly clipped by the viewport.
assets.reviewNote: Accepted on the first build. The first view keyed 28.2% to the studio backdrop, which IS the through-hole; a filled opening would have keyed near the cabinet 5-7%.

assets.role: wall architecture — French Tudor framing mounted beside each exhibit

inputLineage.styleAnchor: public/art/fossil-wall.png — the pavilion exhibit carrying its timber architecture

inspection.optimization: gltf-transform optimize — simplify, quantization, 1024px webp textures. Lossy.

acceptedProperties: One coherent panel; timbers kept their thickness as solid members rather than flattening into painted stripes.
Both diagonal braces genuinely meet the central stud.
Opaque plaster infill, recessed with the timbers standing proud.
Shingled head present.
Warm brown oak, no key-colour contamination, no lettering.
knownLimitations: The central brace/stud joint is fused rather than showing clear joinery.

At the size it renders in-room (~70px wide) the timber detail does not resolve: it reads as a framed rectangular panel rather than as a timber frame. This is a placement and scale problem, not a reconstruction defect — a solid-colour probe confirmed it renders at full size, upright and facing the camera.
assets.reviewNote: The kit highest-risk module and it passed on the first build: an open structural frame reconstructs like a flat surface far more easily than a closed body does.

assets.role: museum furniture — a closed oak cabinet giving human scale and somewhere for relics to live

inputLineage.styleAnchor: public/art/keepers-room.png — the pavilion exhibit carrying its furniture joinery

inspection.optimization: gltf-transform optimize — simplify, quantization, 1024px webp textures. Lossy.

acceptedProperties: One coherent closed carcass; no merged blobs or doubled parts.
Solid opaque panelled oak doors; no glazing and no opening where a door should be.
Projecting cornice and moulded plinth base.
Brass ring pulls and visible hinges.
Warm brown wood with pronounced grain, no lettering.
knownLimitations: Hardware reads as soft lumpy approximations rather than crisp brass fittings.
Texture smearing at the plinth and some glossy streaks in the grain.
The far side of the carcass is unresolved — it is placed angled against the wall, which hides that side.

invariants: Every displayed model is listed here with its generator tasks.
Canonical characters are never generated. Luma's body remains fixed by art/luma-canon.json.
A generated prop carries artistic-interpretation status and never upgrades a room's evidence status.
Lossy optimization is disclosed; the delivered mesh is not presented as the generator's raw output.
A generated asset records its input reference views, not only its task IDs, where the material language came from images rather than a prompt.
